solution:
For a fixed mass, the number of ATOMS is \(\dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{molar mass}} \times N_A \times (\text{atoms per formula unit})\), so the substance with the smallest molar mass per atom wins.

Taking \(1\,\text{g}\) of each and \(N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\):

Gold, \(M = 197\,\text{g mol}^{-1}\), monatomic: \(\dfrac{1}{197} \times N_A = 3.06 \times 10^{21}\) atoms

Sodium, \(M = 23.0\,\text{g mol}^{-1}\), monatomic: \(\dfrac{1}{23.0} \times N_A = 2.62 \times 10^{22}\) atoms

Lithium, \(M = 6.94\,\text{g mol}^{-1}\), monatomic: \(\dfrac{1}{6.94} \times N_A = 8.68 \times 10^{22}\) atoms

Dichlorine, \(M = 70.9\,\text{g mol}^{-1}\), but each molecule carries 2 atoms: \(\dfrac{1}{70.9} \times 2 \times N_A = 1.70 \times 10^{22}\) atoms

Lithium has by far the smallest molar mass, and even the two atoms per \(\text{Cl}_2\) molecule do not make up for chlorine's molar mass being about ten times larger.

Hence \(1\,\text{g}\) of lithium contains the largest number of atoms, \(8.68 \times 10^{22}\).
